messages:
anya: Quick sync — I want to lock down the benchmark methodology for FP8/INT8 runs before the next perf cycle. We keep getting noise from warmup and KV interactions. Can we agree on a deterministic protocol?

matt: +1. TL;DR proposal: 1) explicit KV priming phase, 2) length-stratified batching, 3) power cap + fan fixed, 4) single-tokenization pipeline used for all model variants.

rachel: Agree on the checklist. Also call out calibration randomness for INT8/FP8 — we need fixed seeds and deterministic data slices. Calibration artifacts are changing latency at the kernel level.

noah: Two quick notes from infra: 1) we must pin driver + cuDNN versions in the job; 2) isolate GPU (no other processes, nvidia-smi monitoring only). Otherwise clock/thermal jitter kills reproducibility.

anya: Draft config I used this morning (copied):

```
# benchmark config
model: llama-65b-fp8
variants: [fp8, int8, fp16]
warmup_tokens: 1024
measure_tokens: 8192
batching_policy: length_stratified
batch_sizes: [1,4,8]
power_limit_watts: 220
fan_profile: fixed-75%
driver: 525.60
cuDNN: 8.5
calib_seed: 42
calib_subset_id: fixed-slice-07
kv_mode: persistent  # prime KV, keep across requests
profilers: [nsys, nvprof, perf_event]
```

matt: Nice. A couple clarifications: - "warmup_tokens" should be TWO-phase: fast priming (prefix tokens to populate KV, e.g., 512 tokens) then thermal warmup (continuous steady-state generation for 30s). We should capture both. - batching_policy: length_stratified is best to avoid mixed-length tail effects on kernel selection.

rachel: On calibration: use the exact same corpus and tokenizer for calibration and measurement. Not just same text: same byte offsets. Tokenizer change (BPE/backend) made a 7% throughput delta last week.

anya: Example run commands I've been using:

```
# priming
python bench.py --model $M --mode prime --tokens 512 --kv persistent
# thermal warmup
python bench.py --model $M --mode warmup --duration 30 --power-limit 220
# measurement
python bench.py --model $M --mode measure --tokens 8192 --batch-policy length_stratified --seed 42
```

noah: For power control we use `nvidia-smi -pl 220` + `nvpmodel` locked. Also set `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to the single GPU and kill the node monitoring daemons that schedule background tasks.

perf-bot: PERF RUN STARTED: tid=fp8-2025-10-12-09-13, nodes=1, gpus=1, power_limit=220W. Capturing nsys timeline.

matt: We should capture per-kernel choice logs from the runtime: kernel selector decision + heuristics used (sequence length, batch size, kv-hit-rate). That helps correlate cold-paths where fallback kernels run.

rachel: Add to logging: `kernel_selector{model,seq_len,batch_size,kv_hits,calib_profile}` — timestamped at call sites. Even a CSV is fine.

anya: Perf regressions we saw: FP8 kernels sometimes fall back to FP16 for attention when calibration fails and bias ranges exceed thresholds. That fallback shows up as periodic latency spikes. How to detect automatically?

matt: Detect by comparing per-token kernel tags across the run. If >0.5% tokens use fallback kernel, flag the run. Also track KV cache eviction events — those cause extra forward passes.

noah: On KV: When benchmarking, we must define whether KV is kept hot across the whole measurement or reset per-request. Both are valid, but label the run as `kv_persistent` vs `kv_reset`. Many production workloads keep KV hot.

rachel: For fair comparisons between quant modes: 1) same micro-batch composition (length distribution), 2) same compiler/kernels, 3) same power/fan/clock, 4) repeated trials (N=5) with median reported. Also include 95th percentile tail.

anya: How long between runs? If thermal drift is a concern, we should wait until device power draw and temperature settle within +/-2C. Can we automate that?

noah: Yes. Add a short cooldown probe: poll `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,power.draw` every 5s; continue when last 4 samples within range. We can add this as a preflight check in bench.py.

perf-bot: PERF SAMPLE: fp8 median throughput=210 tok/s, fp16 median throughput=195 tok/s, int8 median=205 tok/s. KV mode=persistent, warmup=2phase. nsys traces uploaded to gs://perf-traces/fp8-2025-10-12-09-13

matt: Good numbers. But check tokenization parity: measure tokens-per-input for each variant to ensure same model inputs yield identical token counts. If not, normalize by tokens or rerun with canonicalized input.

rachel: Also log the calibration histogram for activations (min/max per-channel). If calibration is clipping values often, throughput wins but quality might regress. We need a quality check step in the pipeline (perplexity or end-to-end eval) tied to the same calibration slice.

anya: Proposed final methodology (short):
- Environment: fixed driver/cuDNN, single GPU, power/fan pinned, background processes killed.
- Warmup: two-phase (KV prime tokens, thermal steady-state duration).
- Measurement: length-stratified batches, fixed seed, N=5 runs, report median & 95p.
- KV: label runs as `persistent` or `reset`. For `persistent`, document prime tokens count.
- Calibration: fixed seed + fixed subset; capture calibration histograms.
- Logging: per-kernel selector CSV, KV eviction events, nsys profiles, tokenization parity check, hw probes.
- Fairness: same tokenization pipeline and batch composition for all variants.

noah: I'll implement the preflight cooldown + power pin helper in infra tools tomorrow.

matt: I'll add kernel selector logging hooks in runtime and a small analyzer to flag fallback rates >0.5%.

rachel: I'll wire a small quality check (BLEU/perp) in the pipeline and fail the run if quality drops beyond configured thresholds.

anya: Awesome. Can we treat this as the canonical benchmark protocol and add to the perf playbook? If everyone signs off I'll add the docs + perf CI job. :thumbsup:

matt: :+1:

rachel: :ok_hand:
